<!--
An issue is a prompt. Write it so an agent can pick it up and execute without
asking what you meant. State the desired OUTCOME, not the step-by-step
implementation (unless the implementation itself is the point).

A good issue lets the agent:
  1. understand the problem or goal
  2. know what "done" looks like
  3. verify its own work against the test plan

Delete these HTML comments before submitting — they stay visible while you
write but render invisible in the final issue.
-->

## Problem or desired outcome

<!-- What is wrong, or what should exist after this change? State the outcome. -->

## Context

<!-- What does the agent need: files, prior art, constraints, dependencies, links. -->

## Proposed solution (optional)

<!-- Your hypothesis. Leave room for the agent to challenge it. -->

## Risk tier

<!-- `routine` (fix / small enhancement → main) or `serious` (core logic / data model / template / public interface / high-risk → branch + PR). Add the matching label. -->

## Test plan

<!-- How will we know it worked? Concrete checks the agent can run. -->
